questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Since I am majoring in Agricultural economics for me it was very interesting to learn what role agriculture plays in another continent, country, and economy. Not only, Colombia had and still has a very complicated agricultural panorama due to relatively recent social issues but also because of the coexistence between modern export agriculture, farmer, and indigenous. 
Also the language, I wanted to learn Spanish and escape Danish winter

questions.answer: Quite easy, the international office called ORI was very useful and helpful

questions.answer: Welcome days, ORI office

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not the easiest because I started a bit too late to look for houses, but there is not the worry to not find anything at all like in Copenhagen. I used Airbnb for the first weeks and then VICO. Initally I lived in Zona G but it was a bit far from university and while transportation is good, traffic is mad

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is not a problem at all in terms of safety, you just have to choose a nice neighbourhood. If you go to university everyday and have class early in the morning, you should consider living closer to avoid morning traffic. I was living in Parkway which is more less 30 minutes walk from university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Had to go to my faculty international office and talk to the person in charge which is the one you also exchange emails with when choosing courses

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Course choice guidance, course registration

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Good, just to keep in mind that many classes happen at the same time so do not register for two classes that are at 7 am

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask professors if there are study trips for their courses (study trips are very cool and opportunity to travel basically free) and what kind of examination they require for the completion of the course

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took course of Agroclimatology, Sustainable Agri food systems, and Agroecology. professors very well prepared and insanely good literature that they provided

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's similar in a sense that you have to prepare presentation, write papers and such, but in my opinion it is way more involving the way they teach, the fact that what they teach to students is very actual, tangible problems you see in the economy (in my case agriculture). I was at the faculty of Agricultural science and the professors were all very passionate and with super interesting background, as well very happy to involve you in any initiative if you ask. Plenty of ways to get involved more especially as a foregneir they appreciate it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Agroclimatology, Sustainable Agri food systems, and Agroecology

What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sustainable Agri food systems (sistemas agroalimentarios sustentables) such a good course, interesting content, good literature and the professor such a lovely person

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: dont miss the welcome days thats when you meet all the exchange students

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Salsa classes, singing classes, sport classes of many kind (no swimming), social thursday, agroecological market every first wednesday of the month.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Salsa classes, Social Thursday

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I mean travel as much as you can even if in the beginning you think you have no people to go with. you can also travel alone, its perfectly fine with some sense. Colombia has so much to offer in terms of natural beauty.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: in general very easy, people are lovely and kind especially helpful when they see you are a foreigner. for me that i have never studied spanish before in my life it was a bit hard to connect with people in the beginning but then it was fine

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: id say to ask them for lunch break at uni, ask them if they want to do something with you in the city. be mindful to not ask anyone to travel with you (especially if youre in a public university) because not everyone can afford to travel so thats a bit insensitive.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing really, its just a bit chaotic and noisy all the time but in a good way. its lively and not boring

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The music, people friendliness, food and fruit, beautiful travel spots

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to speak Spanish as much as you can since the beginning, dont be shy or youll never learn. you can take courses with teachers while youre there
Try to socialise with anyone, dont stick to the exchange bubble otherwise itll be like staying in europe (cause its mostly germans and french). try to meet locals, thats how youll learn more about the people/country/culture
Travel and dont wait for others to go with you

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The professors are usually very kind, if you think you also might want a thesis with one of them or want to ask for advice they ll be more than happy to help

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Picking up Spanish. Meeting lovely people and travelling to incredible places. Decentralise myself from the "global north" mentality and arrogance that our way of life is better, safer, tidier, and shinier. Obviously, Colombia like all South America is problematic for different aspects, but it is very far from the jungle people describe where you might get shot or robbed at any moment. that is just lies and we as foreigners are lucky to be able to live in nicer neighbourhoods, so if youre careful thatll never happen to you. didnt get robbed once. Discovering that countries like Colombia and its people have so much to offer and are rising and trying to shake off the ugly reputation they have and we keep labeling them with

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: in the beginning communication really, didnt speak spanish and didnt have time to meet up with a lot of ppl cause i was busy looking for houses

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Save money before going to colombia cause itd be a shame to not explore it. dont try to explore all Latin america, you can stick to just colombia and still have so much to explore after you leave, the list never ends.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
